_comment: Golden meter-identification set: real, attested Sanskrit verses paired with
their traditionally-assigned chandas. Every entry is verified twice:
1. by an INDEPENDENT gana-string expansion (see tests/test_chandas_golden.py
GANAS/_pattern_from_ganas) -- so the golden truth does not depend on
meters-full.csv being right, and disagreements surface as CSV bugs;
2. by slm.rules.ChandasEngine.scan(), which is what the test asserts on.
meter    -- lowercase IAST name, must match meters-full.csv name_iast for
ganas    -- canonical Pingala gana definition, or null for rule-defined
families (anustubh, upajati) that have no single fixed pattern.
syllables-- syllables per pada (null for rule-defined families).
text     -- IAST, one pada per line, no dandas needed.
Sources are listed per entry. Meter attributions cross-checked against
Pingala's Chandahsutra gana definitions and the references in `source_url`.

verses.text:
tapaḥsvādhyāyanirataṃ
tapasvī vāgvidāṃ varam
nāradaṃ paripapraccha
vālmīkir munipuṅgavam
verses.notes: Odd pada a has L L L at syllables 5-7 (na-gana) -- a legal na-vipula, NOT pathya. Regression guard: the epic's own first verse must not be rejected as 'unknown'.

verses.text:
vāgarthāviva saṃpṛktau
vāgarthapratipattaye
jagataḥ pitarau vande
pārvatīparameśvarau
verses.notes: Textbook pathya: 5-6-7 = L G G in odd padas, L G L in even padas.

verses.text:
karmaṇyevādhikāraste
mā phaleṣu kadācana
mā karmaphalaheturbhūr
mā te saṅgo'stvakarmaṇi
verses.notes: 645 of the Gita's 700 verses are anustubh.

verses.text:
vedeṣu yajñeṣu tapaḥsu caiva
dāneṣu yatpuṇyaphalaṃ pradiṣṭam
atyeti tatsarvamidaṃ viditvā
yogī paraṃ sthānamupaiti cādyam
verses.notes: One of only three pure-indravajra verses in the Gita (8.28, 15.5, 15.15). Pada a ends in short 'va' -- pada-final anceps is REQUIRED to match.

verses.text:
nirmānamohā jitasaṅgadoṣā
adhyātmanityā vinivṛttakāmāḥ
dvandvairvimuktāḥ sukhaduḥkhasaṃjñair
gacchantyamūḍhāḥ padamavyayaṃ tat
verses.notes: Pada d ends in short 'tat' -> L; anceps required.

verses.text:
yathā nadīnāṃ bahavo'mbuvegāḥ
samudramevābhimukhā dravanti
tathā tavāmī naralokavīrā
viśanti vaktrāṇyabhivijvalanti
verses.notes: All four padas open with a laghu -> pure upendravajra, not upajati.

verses.text:
vāsāṃsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya
navāni gṛhṇāti naro'parāṇi
tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇāny
anyāni saṃyāti navāni dehī
verses.notes: Padas a/d are indravajra, b/c upendravajra -> genuine mixed upajati. Upajati is 49 of the Gita's 55 non-anustubh verses and cannot be a row in meters-full.csv. Note the pada c/d split falls INSIDE the sandhi jirnani+anyani -> jirnany|anyani, which is why pada c is written ending in -ny.

verses.text:
astyuttarasyāṃ diśi devatātmā
himālayo nāma nagādhirājaḥ
pūrvāparau toyanidhī vagāhya
sthitaḥ pṛthivyā iva mānadaṇḍaḥ
verses.notes: Pada a = indravajra, pada b = upendravajra.

verses.source: Kalidasa, Meghaduta 1.1 -- the locus classicus of mandakranta
verses.ganas: ma bha na ta ta ga ga
verses.text:
kaścit kāntāvirahaguruṇā svādhikārapramattaḥ
śāpenāstaṃgamitamahimā varṣabhogyeṇa bhartuḥ
yakṣaścakre janakatanayāsnānapuṇyodakeṣu
snigdhacchāyātaruṣu vasatiṃ rāmagiryāśrameṣu
verses.notes: The verse Kalidasa is said to have invented the metre for. Yati after syllables 4 and 10.

verses.ganas: ma bha na ta ta ga ga
verses.text:
śāntākāraṃ bhujagaśayanaṃ padmanābhaṃ sureśaṃ
viśvādhāraṃ gaganasadṛśaṃ meghavarṇaṃ śubhāṅgam
lakṣmīkāntaṃ kamalanayanaṃ yogibhirdhyānagamyaṃ
vande viṣṇuṃ bhavabhayaharaṃ sarvalokaikanātham
verses.notes: Very widely recited; independent second witness for mandakranta.

verses.ganas: ma sa ja sa ta ta ga
verses.text:
yā kundendutuṣārahāradhavalā yā śubhravastrāvṛtā
yā vīṇāvaradaṇḍamaṇḍitakarā yā śvetapadmāsanā
yā brahmācyutaśaṅkaraprabhṛtibhirdevaiḥ sadā vanditā
sā māṃ pātu sarasvatī bhagavatī niḥśeṣajāḍyāpahā
verses.notes: Yati after syllable 12.

verses.ganas: ma sa ja sa ta ta ga
verses.text:
kastūrītilakaṃ lalāṭaphalake vakṣaḥsthale kaustubhaṃ
nāsāgre varamauktikaṃ karatale veṇuṃ kare kaṅkaṇam
sarvāṅge haricandanaṃ sulalitaṃ kaṇṭhe ca muktāvalī
gopastrīpariveṣṭito vijayate gopālacūḍāmaṇiḥ
verses.notes: Second independent witness for shardulavikridita.

verses.ganas: ta bha ja ja ga ga
verses.text:
yāṃ cintayāmi satataṃ mayi sā viraktā
sāpyanyamicchati janaṃ sa jano'nyasaktaḥ
asmatkṛte ca pariśuṣyati kācidanyā
dhiktāṃ ca taṃ ca madanaṃ ca imāṃ ca māṃ ca
verses.notes: Vasantatilaka has no obligatory yati.

verses.ganas: ya ma na sa bha la ga
verses.text:
mahimnaḥ pāraṃ te paramaviduṣo yadyasadṛśī
stutirbrahmādīnāmapi tadavasannāstvayi giraḥ
athāvācyaḥ sarvaḥ svamatipariṇāmāvadhi gṛṇan
mamāpyeṣa stotre hara nirapavādaḥ parikaraḥ
verses.notes: Yati after syllable 6.

verses.text:
bhagavati tava tīre nīramātrāśano'haṃ
vigataviṣayatṛṣṇaḥ kṛṣṇamārādhayāmi
sakalakaluṣabhaṅge svargasopānasaṅge
taralatarataraṅge devi gaṅge prasīda
verses.notes: Opens with five laghus -- malini's signature.

verses.text:
manobuddhyahaṅkāracittāni nāhaṃ
na ca śrotrajihve na ca ghrāṇanetre
na ca vyoma bhūmirna tejo na vāyuḥ
cidānandarūpaḥ śivo'haṃ śivo'ham
verses.notes: Four ya-ganas (L G G x4).

verses.ganas: ja ra ja ra ja ga
verses.text:
jaṭāṭavīgalajjalapravāhapāvitasthale
galevalambya lambitāṃ bhujaṅgatuṅgamālikām
ḍamaḍḍamaḍḍamaḍḍamannināda vaḍḍamarvayaṃ
cakāra caṇḍatāṇḍavaṃ tanotu naḥ śivaḥ śivam
verses.notes: Strict L-G alternation, 16 syllables. meters-full.csv currently lists pañcacāmara as 12 syllables (LGLGLGLGLGLG) -- that row is WRONG; canonical is ja ra ja ra ja ga = 16.

verses.ganas: ma ra bha na ya ya ya
verses.text:
yā sṛṣṭiḥ sraṣṭurādyā vahati vidhihutaṃ yā havir yā ca hotrī
ye dve kālaṃ vidhattaḥ śrutiviṣayaguṇā yā sthitā vyāpya viśvam
yāmāhuḥ sarvabījaprakṛtiriti yayā prāṇinaḥ prāṇavantaḥ
pratyakṣābhiḥ prapannastanubhiravatu vastābhiraṣṭābhirīśaḥ
verses.notes: Longest metre in regular use. Yati after syllables 7 and 14.

verses.text:
dṛṣṭavadānuśravikaḥ sa hyaviśuddhikṣayātiśayayuktaḥ
tadviparītaḥ śreyānvyaktāvyaktajñavijñānāt
verses.notes: Jati (moraic), not aksharachandas: 57 matras split 12/18/12/15, with NO fixed syllable pattern -- this verse is 35 syllables, another arya may be 30. The whole Samkhyakarika is in arya. Written as 2 lines (the conventional half-verse layout), so pada_count is 2, not 4.

verses.text:
duḥkhatrayābhighātājjijñāsā tadapaghātake hetau
dṛṣṭe sāpārthā cennaikāntātyantato'bhāvāt
verses.notes: Adversarial case: this arya happens to have 32 syllables, exactly an anustubh's count. sanskrit/chandas misfiles it as 'sloka' because its sloka entry is the all-wildcard pattern '........' and matches any 32-syllable verse. Our anustubh check enforces the 5-7 pathya/vipula rules, so pada d (L G G in an even pada) rejects it and it correctly falls through to the jati test.

irregular.text:
kālo'smi lokakṣayakṛtpravṛddho
lokānsamāhartumiha pravṛttaḥ
ṛte'pi tvāṃ na bhaviṣyanti sarve
ye'vasthitāḥ pratyanīkeṣu yodhāḥ
scansion: LGGGLLGGLGG  vatormi with a laghu opening -- not upendravajra
irregular.reason: Held OUT of the graded set on purpose. Popular sources call this verse upajati, but only two of its four padas are classical indravajra; the other two follow the looser epic/Vedic tristubh licence (11 syllables + fixed cadence, free interior). Grading a strict classical identifier against it would be scoring the engine on a claim the text does not support. Kept here as documentation of a real, common input the engine will honestly return 'unknown' for.

unsupported.source: giti / upagiti / udgiti / aryagiti / vaitaliya / matrasamaka
unsupported.meter: the rest of the jāti (mora-counting) families
unsupported.reason: ChandasEngine.JATIS holds only arya (12/18/12/15). The mechanism -- _jati(), mora prefix-sums -- generalises to the other jatis by adding rows, but each needs an attested golden verse first: a jati rule is far looser than a fixed L/G pattern, so an unverified row can shadow real vrtta matches. Adding one without a test would trade a known gap for an unknown regression.
